- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; increase forecast to align with recent downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–67), model tends to ignore it; adjust downward by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out 3–5 day moving average before final output.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles, model tends to misalign with trend direction; favor sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days.
